title: Shannon separated information from meaning
body: Claude E. Shannon's 1948 paper "A Mathematical Theory of Communication," in the Bell System Technical Journal, defines a quantity for the information produced by a source. The measure depends on how uncertain the next message is, not on whether the message is important to a person. A rare message carries more information, in this sense, than a message the receiver already expects. Shannon entropy is that measure. The theory then asks how much of it can be sent through a noisy channel. Meaning, truth, and persuasion are outside the theory on purpose. A channel can carry a lie as efficiently as a fact. The paper is the foundation of digital communication engineering. It is not a theory of semantics, and using "information" in Shannon's sense and in the ordinary sense in the same sentence is a common confusion.
said_by: Claude E. Shannon, Bell System Technical Journal, 1948
